title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Budget cut for Head U
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head U of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head U of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Evolution and adaptation of the Public Service.

sections.label: Issues dominating Public Sector work
sections.summary: Demographic changes, gender mainstreaming, economic transformation, safety and security technology, and becoming a Smart Nation will dominate Public Sector work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Issues such as: (a) our demographic changes and the rapidly ageing populace; (b) gender mainstreaming and equality that we all want to see; (c) the economic transformation; (d) maintaining safety and security using the latest technology; and (e) our journey towards becoming a Smart Nation will dominate work in the Public Sector.

sections.label: Preparing officers for technological disruptions
sections.summary: It asks how Public Service officers are prepared for technological disruptions like AI and VR while remaining comfortable with face-to-face communication.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How are we preparing our Public Service officers for all these – the technological disruptions – with the use of artificial intelligence (AI), virtual reality (VR) ways of handling issues and yet still keep them comfortable and acing the face-to-face human correspondence and communications that they need to do with the various sectors, including the public?

sections.label: Masterplan to transform Public Service
sections.summary: It asks whether a masterplan similar to the 23 Industry Transformation Maps exists to transform the Public Service into a smarter Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, just as the Government rolls out the 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) to transform our industries, is there a similar masterplan to transform our Public Service to be a smarter Government?

sections.label: KPIs for large budget Ministries
sections.summary: It asks whether large budget Ministries could get industry development and job creation KPIs, noting citizens' acute demand for speed, effectiveness and transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could all large budget Ministries be given industry development and job creation key performance indicators (KPIs)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Public Service may not be the first that comes to mind to be associated with the words "speed" and "innovation", but citizens' demand for greater speed, effectiveness and transparency in public service delivery is increasingly acute.

sections.label: Bureaucracy, incentives and risk-taking
sections.summary: It asks whether being citizen-centric is hindered by bureaucracy, lack of incentives to innovate, or being too quick to penalise risk-taking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In finding this balance, we must ask ourselves audibly from time to time, in our bid to be citizen-centric, are we stymied by bureaucracy or a lack of incentives from the service to innovate or being too quick to penalise risk-taking?

sections.label: Rules, discretion, public servant appraisal
sections.summary: Warns against hiding behind rules while ignoring them for customer satisfaction, and asks if PMO will consider 360-degree appraisal for public servants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A danger is that we will take refuge behind increasing rules and regulations so as to deal with complexity, but to disregard these in the pursuit of short term "customer satisfaction" as online mass agitation becomes ever louder and pervasive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Even as we find ways to increase the productivity and responsiveness of our officers, we must also enable them with skill and discretion, to say no to unreasonable requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) consider implementing a 360-degree appraisal review system for all public servants?

sections.label: Guidelines for public consultation on Bills
sections.summary: Asks whether guidelines or SOPs exist on when public consultation on a Bill is required, its period, citing the Films (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask if there is a guideline or standard operating procedure (SOP) on how Ministries should approach law-making.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When is public consultation on a Bill a must and when is public consultation deemed not needed?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Are there any guidelines about the consultation period?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The recent consultation on the Films (Amendment) Bill illustrates the problem when the consultation period was too short, initially for a period of about 11 days in the month of December, which is generally a month where persons may also travel.

sections.label: Government claiming relief under POHA
sections.summary: Cites a 2017 Court case where the Government tried to claim it was a person entitled to seek relief under POHA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One recent example is the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) when, in a 2017 Court case, the Government tried to claim that it was a person entitled to seek relief under POHA.

sections.label: Public Service innovation
sections.summary: States that the cut is to discuss whether the Public Service can be more innovative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, my cut today is to discuss whether our Public Service can be more innovative.

sections.label: Tax increase and public sector efficiency
sections.summary: Says another reason for the public sector to improve efficiency and productivity is that a tax increase has been announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Another important reason for the public sector to improve efficiency and productivity, as many of my colleagues have pointed out, is the fact that a tax increase has been announced.

sections.label: Digital economy and Moments of Life
sections.summary: Says the digital economy offers more avenues for citizens to interact with Government, citing the announced Moments of Life project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The digital economy offers even more avenues for citizens to interact with the Government in ways that were not possible in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There is this "Moments of Life" project, a strategic initiative that bundles relevant Government services across all agencies based on milestones of a citizen's life, that has been announced.

sections.label: Whistleblowing routes for public servants
sections.summary: MP asks whether civil servants are clearly told they can report lapses in good faith to PSC, and whether PSC is the reporting point and resourced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, based on a Parliamentary exchange in 2012, other than the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) and Auditor-General, Public Service officers can direct whistleblowing complaints to PSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is it currently made clear to all civil and public servants that they can highlight problematic acts without fear for their careers, provided that the reporting is in good faith?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Also, is PSC the whistleblower reporting point for ethical lapses for the whole Public Service, including for lapses relating to the recent requirement that a political officeholder cannot instruct the civil servants to act with respect to a person or persons and, if so, is the PSC properly resourced to handle such complaints?

sections.label: Government Technology Agency inauguration
sections.summary: GovTech's inauguration signals the Government's drive towards growth, innovation and productivity, and it aims to support Smart Nation projects and rejuvenate e-Government services.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The inauguration of Government Technology Agency (GovTech) is a clear signal to show the Government’s drive towards growth, innovation and productivity in the digital world and future economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: GovTech aims to provide engineering support to Smart Nation projects as well as to rejuvenate old e-Government services.

sections.label: Benchmark for Ministerial salaries
sections.summary: Ministerial salaries were benchmarked to the median salary of the top 1,000 income earners, with a 40% discount applied to reflect public service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The benchmark adopted by this House for setting Ministerial salaries was to use the median salary of the top 1,000 income earners, as it was anticipated that people with the calibre to be Ministers and managing large budgets of hundreds of millions of dollars should be comparable to this group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, a 40% discount was applied to this benchmark to indicate that this was public service and people should not come forward for money.

sections.label: Question on five-year review
sections.summary: The speaker asks Deputy Prime Minister Teo whether the Government has conducted a review, given the five-year mark has passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given that we have passed the five-year mark, I would like to ask Deputy Prime Minister Teo whether the Government has conducted a review.

sections.label: Ministerial salaries benchmark introduced 1994
sections.summary: A benchmark for Ministerial salaries was first introduced in 1994 to keep salaries competitive to attract people of the right calibre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To ensure an honest and competent government, a benchmark for Ministerial salaries was first introduced in 1994 to ensure that salaries were kept competitive to attract people of the right calibre to step forward to lead the country.

sections.label: Ministerial salaries review and ITMs
sections.summary: The benchmark was finetuned and last reviewed in this House in 2012, with a review recommended at the five-year mark; 23 ITMs have been launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The benchmark for public officeholders was finetuned subsequently and the last review was carried out in this House in 2012, agreed to by this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Committee to Review the Ministerial Salaries that recommended benchmarks also recommended a review at the five-year mark, which we have since crossed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To date, 23 ITMs have been launched focusing on creating jobs for Singaporeans in various strategic industries.

sections.label: Skills over paper qualifications
sections.summary: It states that officers without graduate degrees can be eligible for similar opportunities and move to higher responsibility if they perform well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It also provides better coordination among different stakeholders of building projects, thus enhancing productivity and reduce wastages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means that officers without graduate degrees can be eligible for similar opportunities as graduates and can move up to higher positions of responsibility if they perform well.

sections.label: Civil Service hiring progress update
sections.summary: Mr Patrick Tay asks for a progress update on Civil Service efforts to focus on skills and competencies rather than paper qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Patrick Tay, you can take your two cuts together, please.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I wish to ask for a progress update on the Civil Service's efforts on not focusing on paper qualifications alone but instead on the applicants' and staff's relevant skills and competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is with respect to new entrants, mid-career and older workers in areas of recruitment, selection, salaries, promotion, re-employment and career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am particularly concerned in light of the number of mature and re-employed workers in the Civil Service as well as the focus on paper qualifications in the hiring of many of these entry level positions at Career@GOV.

sections.label: Collaboration and officer effectiveness
sections.summary: It asks the Minister in charge of the Civil Service how all officers, especially experienced ones, will remain effective and engaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We cannot work in silos and there must be greater collaboration across agencies and the eradication of duplication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister in charge of the Civil Service how the Public Service could ensure that all officers, especially those who are more experienced and perhaps more used to the way things were, will remain effective in their roles and remain fully engaged.

sections.label: Political salary scheme decision
sections.summary: The committee found the scheme relevant and sound, but the Government decided to maintain the current salary structure and level.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The committee's conclusion is that the scheme remains relevant and sound.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: But the committee recommended adjusting the salary levels to match the updated benchmark and also some finetuning on the National Bonus conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Government has decided that since the scheme remains valid and the economy is still in transition, we will not change anything now and will maintain the current salary structure and level.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will review the matter again after five years or when it becomes necessary.

sections.label: Benchmark, bonus and NCMP allowances
sections.summary: It states the Government decided not to change salaries, National Bonus indicators or NCMP allowances, which remain at current levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: On this, the committee noted that the benchmark has increased by 9% since 2011 or a compounded growth rate of 1.5% per year over this period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: But there has been no adjustment made to political salaries over the period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Two, to review the ranges for the National Bonus indicators to take into consideration changing economic conditions and national outlook and, three, to adjust the allowances for Non-Constituency MPs (NCMPs) from 15% of the allowance for elected MPs to 20% to recognise that NCMP have full voting rights in Parliament, from April 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As I have stated earlier, the Prime Minister has written to the committee to thank the committee for its work and its well-considered recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: However, the Government has decided not to make any changes and to maintain the current salary structure and level.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: While the MR4 benchmark has increased by 9% since 2011, or the compounded growth rate of 1.5% per year over this period, the Government knows that the 2017 MR4 benchmark is lower than the 2016 MR4 benchmark.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government has decided to maintain salaries at the current level and watch the salary trends further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Government has also decided to maintain the current National Bonus indicators and not make refinements to the wages for the National Bonus indicators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Government has also decided to maintain NCMP allowances at the current level and consider any change where other adjustments need to be made.

sections.label: No change to salaries
sections.summary: The committee recommended a 9% salary adjustment and framework refinements, but the Government decided to maintain the current framework and level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The committee has also recommended that salaries be adjusted by 9%, together with some refinements in the elements within the framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Government has decided not to make any changes now and to maintain the current salary framework and salary level.

sections.label: Internal disclosure framework cases
sections.summary: About 320 cases were reported to the internal disclosure framework in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: About 320 cases were reported to the internal disclosure framework in 2017.

sections.label: Digital capabilities and officer skills
sections.summary: It sets out raising public agencies' digital capabilities and deepening Public Service officers' skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: First, raising the digital capabilities of our Public agencies; and second, deepening the skills of our Public Service officers.

sections.label: HDB resale flat completion time
sections.summary: Buyers and sellers of HDB resale flats can now complete the process in eight weeks since the start of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Buyers and sellers of HDB resale flats can now complete the process in half the time, or just eight weeks, since the start of this year.

sections.label: Training public officers in digital capabilities
sections.summary: Over 4,000 officers attended training by end-2017, and the Civil Service College will partner Institutes of Higher Learning to expand reach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Last year, I spoke about training 10,000 public officers by 2020 in digital capabilities, such as data analytics and data science, for policy formulation, service delivery and corporate services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: More than 4,000 officers have attended training courses as at the end of 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: To expand our reach, the Civil Service College will partner Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) so that every public officer can deepen their skills and have access to tools for this digital age.

sections.label: Public Service employee numbers
sections.summary: The Public Service and its 145,000 employees are no exception.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Public Service and its 145,000 employees are no exception.

sections.label: Public servants' buy-in to policy
sections.summary: Public officers are by and large committed to policies set by the elected Government, in answer to Ms Chia Yong Yong's question.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, Ministers and the Public Service work closely together to continue to deliver public housing, healthcare, education, transport, maintain law and order, keep Singapore safe and secure, attract investments, regulate various sectors, ensure social mobility and so on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, to Ms Chia Yong Yong’s question whether public servants have buy-in to Government policy, I would say, by and large, public officers are committed to policies set by the elected Government.

sections.label: Citizen Engagement Seed Fund
sections.summary: The Citizen Engagement Seed Fund, set up in 2016, has supported 16 projects by agencies that created new citizen participation opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, the Citizen Engagement Seed Fund was set up in 2016 to encourage agencies to trial innovative engagement approaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This fund has supported 16 projects by various agencies which have created new opportunities for citizen participation.

sections.label: Ministry-determined consultation scope and duration
sections.summary: Each Ministry determines the extent, approach and duration of consultation based on factors such as the nature of the amendment, impact and public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The extent and approach to consultation and the duration of consultation, however, are determined by each Ministry, depending on factors, such as the nature of the legislative amendment, impact of the changes and also the level of public interest.

sections.label: Health365 App and CPF service
sections.summary: The Health365 App acts as a fitness buddy, and the CPF Board's Retirement Planning Service uses technology to give personalised CPF advice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, the Health Promotion Board's Health365 App is like a fitness buddy to us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board has launched a CPF Retirement Planning Service, where frontline officers use technology to transform citizens’ data into personalised infographics to provide citizens with personalised advice on CPF matters.

sections.label: Exercise started in 2012
sections.summary: An exercise started in 2012 to serve the public better and be ready for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: An exercise has started in 2012 in order to serve the public better and be ready for the future.

sections.label: Feedback, awards and bonus recognition
sections.summary: Regular 360-degree feedback, the Public Sector Transformation Award, and a bonus mechanism recognise officers' constructive discontent, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One of which is regular 360-degree feedback, to better develop our Public Service leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have also put in place a system, such as the Public Sector Transformation Award, to recognise officers who display constructive discontent, and make the effort to effect transformative change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have also recently incorporated into the bonus system a mechanism for agencies to specifically recognise officers for their innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: Escalating unsupportive supervisor issues
sections.summary: Officers may inform their Permanent Secretary, the Head of the Civil Service, or the speaker if an unsupportive supervisor blocks improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If it is something that makes things better but their immediate supervisor is not supportive, then inform their Permanent Secretary or the Head of the Civil Service, or have a word with me, and I will see to it.

sections.label: Public Service appraisal based on performance
sections.summary: The Public Service appraisal system is based on performance and skills, with past academic results having no bearing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The behaviour of employers plays a big part to engender this culture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, the appraisal system in the Public Service is based on performance and demonstration of skills and competencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: A public officer is recognised based on his contribution and delivery of results, with past academic results having no bearing.

sections.label: Recruiting on passion and skills
sections.summary: Recruitment should be based on passion, skills and aptitudes, and schemes for diploma and degree holders could be merged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Instead, we should continue to recruit based on the applicant's passion, skills and aptitudes for the specific vocation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, one change that we can implement for such skills-based jobs is to merge existing schemes for diploma and degree holders.

sections.label: ATCOs same grade and salaries
sections.summary: Since July 2017, ATCOs with the required skills are placed in the same grade and receive the same salaries regardless of qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since July 2017, all ATCOs, regardless of their academic qualifications, will be placed to the same grade and receive the same salaries once they are assessed and found to have the skills required for the job.

sections.label: New work-learn programme for SWAs
sections.summary: From the second half of this year, SkillsFuture Singapore, SUSS and Nanyang Polytechnic will introduce a work-learn programme for SWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From the second half of this year, SkillsFuture Singapore, the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) and Nanyang Polytechnic will introduce a new work-learn programme for SWAs.

sections.label: Parks linked into one big park
sections.summary: NParks is linking parks through an island-wide Park Connector Network and integrating public facilities, digitalised tree information and tilt sensors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From just providing a park near where you live, they are linking all the parks now through an island-wide Park Connector Network (PCN) so that they become one big park accessible to all.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In recent years, NParks has integrated into parks, public facilities, such as the Woodlands Integrated Healthcare Cluster, the Singapore Armed Forces Reservists' Association (SAFRA) Clubhouse at Chua Chu Kang, and the Singapore Institute of Technology Campus in Punggol.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In Sembawang, it stepped forward to undertake the sprucing up of the only hot spring in Singapore into a Hot Spring Park for the public to enjoy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, information of trees is now captured in a digitalised platform, accessible on officers' mobile devices, and sensors are now being trialled and installed to detect tilt in trees so that mitigating measures can be taken early by the NParks officers.

sections.label: Certifications in arboriculture and horticulture
sections.summary: About one third of them hold certifications in arboriculture, horticulture and park management.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: About one third of them hold certifications in arboriculture, horticulture and park management.

sections.label: Low birth rates and immigration
sections.summary: Young people are needed for the economy and to support older people, but birth rates have stayed around TFR 1.2 and immigration must be measured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Young people are needed for a dynamic economy and to support older people who are living longer lives, some of which are years of poor health, resulting in high medical costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, our birth rates have been low, hovering around the TFR of 1.2 for years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Immigration can only be implemented at a measured pace because social integration and cultural assimilation can pose challenges.

sections.label: Economic growth and ageing costs
sections.summary: Balanced growth and low taxes are partly due to international firms and talent, but ageing and social spending could upset this balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have achieved balanced and inclusive economic growth, provide substantive benefits to our people, while holding taxes relatively low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is partially because we attract international firms and talent which contribute significantly to Singapore's economy while shifting considerable tax burden away from Singaporeans, including the GST that we talked about earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But our ageing population and the accompanying increase in social spending could knock us off our current balance.

sections.label: Transient workforce supporting growth
sections.summary: Singapore's growth has been supported by organic population growth and a sizeable transient workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Historically, Singapore's growth has, therefore, been supported not only by organic population growth, but also by a sizeable transient workforce.

sections.label: Singapore's low total fertility rate
sections.summary: Despite praise for parenting, Singapore's TFR continues to be low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, despite all the joys of extolling the wonders of parenting, our TFR continues to be low in Singapore.

sections.label: Ageing population and GDP drag
sections.summary: Studies project seniors matching or exceeding young residents, 91 elderly per 100 working-age Singaporeans by 2080, and a 1.5 percentage point GDP drag.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to a recent study by the United Overseas Bank (UOB), 2018 will see, for the first time in our history, the percentage of our population aged 65 and older, matching those younger than 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At this rate, seniors will more than double the percentage of our youngest residents in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Researchers from the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) estimated there will be 91 elderly citizens for every 100 working-age Singaporeans by 2080.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If fertility rates in Singapore remain at current levels, the study projects that the ageing population will cause a drag of 1.5 percentage points on per capita GDP growth every year until 2060.

sections.label: Paternity and maternity leave changes
sections.summary: Working dads got two weeks paid compulsory paternity leave, and mothers can share up to four of 16 weeks of paid maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government announced that working dads would finally get two weeks of paid compulsory paternity leave where they used to be entitled to one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government also legislated for working mothers to go from sharing just one of their 16 weeks of paid maternity leave to sharing up to four weeks with their husbands.

sections.label: Sharing maternity leave with husbands
sections.summary: The speaker says this would help families decide what suits their context and wanted working mothers to share up to eight of 16 weeks of paid maternity leave with husbands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This would help families to make the decisions that are most appropriate for their context.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was going to actually just push for having working mothers share up to eight weeks of their 16 weeks of paid maternity leave with their husbands.

sections.label: Public sector infant leave pilot
sections.summary: Josephine Teo announced a three-year pilot giving public sector officers and spouses four weeks unpaid infant leave per parent, and the speaker asks for an update.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the 2017 COS, then Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo announced that the Government was undergoing a three-year pilot where Public Sector officers and their spouses would be given an additional four weeks of unpaid infant leave per parent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: She mentioned that the length of the pilot was necessary for the National Population and Talent Division (NPTD) to test the impact of longer parental leave in a variety of work settings and that NPTD will be using this experience to get a clearer idea of whether a nationwide rollout was feasible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I hope the Second Minister can give an update to the House of any useful insights that have already emerged from the pilot.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up rates
sections.summary: The speaker says paternity leave is close to his heart and states take-up was 44% in 2015 and 38.5% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: So, paternity leave is close to my heart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: I know that the take-up rate for paternity leave in Singapore was 44% in 2015 and 38.5% in 2014.

sections.label: Two-week paternity leave take-up
sections.summary: The speaker asks about 2017 take-up after government-paid paternity leave was extended to two weeks and why it remains under 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: What about for 2017 when Government-paid paternity leave was further extended to two weeks?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Since the period of it taken by fathers is generally much shorter than those taken by mothers, why is the take-up rate of paternity leave still less than 50%?

sections.label: Work-Life Grant and flexible work
sections.summary: The speaker notes 1,500 companies benefited from the Work-Life Grant since 2013 and asks why flexible work arrangements are not more prevalent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I am glad to hear that since its launch in 2013, 1,500 companies have benefited from the Work-Life Grant which provides funding and incentives for companies to offer flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, I am puzzled as to why, based on the 2016 survey when about eight in 10 companies are willing to let their employees go on a planned time-off or to telework to attend to personal matters and one or two companies are willing to let their employees work from home on certain days of the week, FWAs are not more prevalent in Singapore's workplaces.

sections.label: Companies implementing flexi-work schemes
sections.summary: The passage states that in recent years a number of companies have implemented flexi-work schemes letting employees start and end work within agreed times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In recent years, a number of companies have implemented flexi-work schemes where employees can choose to start and end work within a range of agreed times.

sections.label: Housing, preschool and family support
sections.summary: Progress in public housing and preschool provision has helped families, and the passage asks how Government and companies can better support work and family aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the public housing front, significant progress has been made in housing to support couples that start a family early, and enhancements made in preschool provision have also helped dual-income families better manage the education needs of their young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How can the Government better support work and family aspirations, and encourage private sector companies to introduce more family-friendly workplace policies?

sections.label: Strengthening integration and cohesion
sections.summary: The passage asks what more can be done to strengthen integration and bring about greater cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What more can be done to strengthen integration and bring about greater cohesion?

sections.label: Support for couples and ART
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will provide more support for couples, such as enhancing assisted reproduction technology co-funding or raising the age limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Will the Government provide more support for these couples, such as through enhancing assisted reproduction technology co-funding or raising the age limit to 40 years and above?

sections.label: Long-term population strategies
sections.summary: The passage sets out three goals for Singapore's population: a vibrant economy, a cohesive society, and a stable citizen population with strong national identity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to take a longer-term view and share more broadly about how our population strategies prepare us for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We want to work towards a Singapore population that can, one, support a vibrant economy, so Singaporeans can earn a good living; two, enable a cohesive society, where people from different backgrounds can live in harmony; and three, sustain a stable citizen population over the long term, where citizens have a strong sense of national identity.

sections.label: Ageing and low TFR
sections.summary: The passage states two long-term challenges: a rapidly ageing population and a low total fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the same time, we face two long-term challenges as we shape our strategies: first, a rapidly ageing population; second, our low TFR, which many MPs have spoken about.

sections.label: Health, employment and retirement sums
sections.summary: The passage states Singaporeans live an average of 74 years in good health, many older residents are employed, and most active CPF members can set aside the Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, Singaporeans are living an average of 74 years in good health, compared to 67 years three decades ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: More than four in 10 residents aged 65 to 69 are employed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: About six in 10 of active CPF members are now able to set aside the Basic Retirement Sum in their Retirement Accounts when they turn 55.

sections.label: Women's marriage and first birth ages
sections.summary: The median age of Singaporean women at first marriage and at first birth has risen, and conceiving becomes harder after 35.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Two decades ago, the median age of Singaporean women at first marriage was around 26.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The median age of mothers at first birth has accordingly increased from 28.6 to 30.5.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, couples who marry later are more likely to face difficulties conceiving.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Medically, it is well-established that one's chances of conceiving diminish sharply after the age of 35.

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Package investment
sections.summary: Since 2001, significant resources have been invested in a comprehensive Marriage and Parenthood Package.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since 2001, we have invested significant resources in a comprehensive Marriage and Parenthood Package.

sections.label: New BTO flats and shorter waits
sections.summary: Over 50,000 new BTO flats launched since 2015, with 1,100 shorter-wait flats this year and 2,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since 2015, more than 50,000 new BTO flats have been launched, with priority allocation for first-timers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To provide faster access to housing, HDB will start to launch 1,100 flats with shorter waiting times of around two and a half years this year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And I understand that there is another batch of 2,000 to be launched in 2019.

sections.label: New full-day preschool places
sections.summary: Over the next five years, 40,000 new full-day preschool places will be added to meet parents' needs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over the next five years, there will be 40,000 new full-day preschool places to meet the needs of parents.

sections.label: Paternity Leave take-up rates
sections.summary: Since Paternity Leave was introduced five years ago, take-up rates have risen from 25% to 46%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since Paternity Leave was introduced five years ago, take-up rates have increased from 25% to 46%.

sections.label: ART co-funding and MediShield Life extension
sections.summary: ART co-funding support rises from 1 April 2018, and MediShield Life will cover serious pregnancy and delivery complications.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, eligible couples receive co-funding of 75% of the costs of Assisted Reproduction Technology (ART) treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From 1 April 2018, we will raise the maximum support available, from $6,300 to $7,700 for fresh cycles; and from $1,200 to $2,200 for frozen cycles.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, all newborn citizens receive a MediSave grant of $4,000 that can cover their MediShield Life premiums up to age 21.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will go further and extend MediShield Life to cover serious pregnancy and delivery-related complications so that expectant parents can have less to worry about.

sections.label: New Tripartite Standard caregiving leave
sections.summary: A new Tripartite Standard is introduced to encourage employers to provide caregiving leave in such instances.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our fourth enhancement is to introduce a new Tripartite Standard to encourage employers to provide caregiving leave in such instances.

sections.label: Workforce growth till 2020
sections.summary: From now till 2020, workforce growth will be around 1% to 2% per year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From now till 2020, workforce growth will be around 1% to 2% per year.

sections.label: Singapore Citizenships granted last year
sections.summary: Last year, 22,076 Singapore Citizenships were granted, about the same as in the past few years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Last year, 22,076 Singapore Citizenships were granted, about the same as in the past few years.

sections.label: Immigration policy and replacement TFR
sections.summary: Between the two dotted lines, the situation can mimic replacement TFR, so no major immigration policy changes are expected presently.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members will see that between those two dotted lines, we will be able to mimic the situation as if we have replacement TFR.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, we do not expect any major changes to our immigration policy presently.

sections.label: PR population and PRs granted
sections.summary: The PR population remains largely stable at around 530,000, with 31,849 PRs granted last year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The PR population remains largely stable at around 530,000, with 31,849 PRs granted last year.

sections.label: Council supported integration projects
sections.summary: Over the past three years, the Council under Minister Grace Fu has supported more than 320 ground-up integration projects by 150 organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over the past three years, the Council, under the leadership of Minister Grace Fu, has supported more than 320 ground-up integration projects by 150 organisations.

sections.label: Population and infrastructure plans
sections.summary: Agencies plan new towns and rail lines, with total population likely below six million by 2020 and significantly below 6.9 million by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Agencies have been planning ahead to create a vibrant and endearing Home in which Singaporeans can live, work and play.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These include plans to build new towns, such as Tengah and Bidadari, and extend our rail networks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Downtown Line has fully opened, and more lines, such as the Thomson-East Coast Line, Jurong Region Line and Cross-Island Line, are on the way.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Given recent trends in foreign employment and the current pace of immigration, we expect that (a) by 2020, total population is likely to be below six million; (b) by 2030, the total population is likely to be significantly below 6.9 million, as Prime Minister Lee announced previously.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our long-term infrastructure plans are well in place and being steadily implemented.

sections.label: Goals for 2030 and beyond
sections.summary: The passage lists goals for 2030 and beyond: a great home, vibrant economy, open yet cohesive society, and quality infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Together, we can work towards a bright future in 2030 and beyond: (a) where Singapore remains a great home to build families and grow old together; (b) where our economy is vibrant and able to create good jobs for Singaporeans; (c) where society is open yet cohesive; and (d) where there is quality infrastructure to meet our needs.

sections.label: Smart Nation initiatives since 2014
sections.summary: Since the Prime Minister launched the Smart Nation initiative in 2014, various initiatives have been implemented and embedded within ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, since the Prime Minister launched the Smart Nation initiative in 2014, we have seen various initiatives implemented and many of these elements are already embedded within various ITMs.

sections.label: Smart Nation and Digital Government Group
sections.summary: The Smart Nation and Digital Government Group was formed last year under PMO to bring Government tech agencies and teams together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, the Smart Nation and Digital Government Group (SNDGG) was formed last year under PMO to bring together under one umbrella all the various Government tech agencies and teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can PMO update us on how the approach towards Smart Nation has evolved under SNDGG?

sections.label: Goal for social assistance applications
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that applicants for social assistance or Government schemes need not provide documentation if data already exists in Government systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As we drive more digital services in Government, I would like to propose a goal that any applicant for social assistance or Government schemes should not be required to provide any documentation if the data already exists within the Government systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Better yet, if we can put a goal to reduce processing time for all social assistance or financial scheme applications by a significant proportion as a result.

sections.label: Updates on SNIs and targets
sections.summary: The passage asks for updates on SNIs, progress in software and hardware, targets to 2020 and beyond, and comparison with other nations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can we have an update on our SNIs and how much progress we are making in terms of software and hardware, including our data and tech infrastructure investment plans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What are the targets for the next three years to 2020 and beyond?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How far ahead are we, compared with other nations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What else must we do to ensure that we are not left behind?

sections.label: Smart Nation projects benefits
sections.summary: Asks how the Smart Nation Strategic National Projects have benefited Singaporeans and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How have the Smart Nation Strategic National Projects benefited Singaporeans and businesses?

sections.label: Big data privacy concerns
sections.summary: Asks whether individual privacy concerns should be borne in mind when data is used without prior informed consent.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While big data, granted, has an enormous potential to improve public services and business productivity, should we not bear in mind that there are also individual privacy concerns when data is used in new tech applications, services and research without our mindful, prior informed consent?

sections.label: UK Parliament select committee
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government, PMO and agencies will consider following the UK Parliament's establishment of a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of all of these, I would like to ask: will the Government, PMO and the relevant agencies consider taking a leaf from the UK Parliament which, a few years ago, established a Select Committee for this purpose?

sections.label: National Strategic Projects progress
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to update on progress in the five main areas of the National Strategic Projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: SNI involves the National Strategic Projects which cover five main areas, such as National Digital Identity, e-payments and Moments of Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Minister update on the progress in these five main areas?

sections.label: E-payment systems free market
sections.summary: States that waiting for free market forces to reduce e-payment systems might take too long.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, waiting for free market forces to reduce the number of e-payment systems might take too long because of substantial installed base effect and innovation resistance.

sections.label: Government industry collective effort
sections.summary: Asks PMO how the Government will work with industry and what outcomes citizens and industries can expect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It needs to be a collective effort among the Government, citizens and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask PMO: how is the Government going to work with the industry?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And what tangible outcomes can citizens and industries expect?

sections.label: Smart Nation economy and jobs
sections.summary: The passage asks how Smart Nation can contribute further to Singapore's economy and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can PMO share more about how Smart Nation can contribute further to Singapore’s economy and jobs?

sections.label: E-payments adoption rate
sections.summary: The passage asks what the adoption rate for e-payments is right now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: On e-payments, what is the adoption rate right now?

sections.label: SNI launch and aims
sections.summary: SNI was launched in late 2014 to apply digital and smart solutions for better services to residents and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, SNI was launched in late 2014 with the aim of applying digital and smart solutions to provide better services to our residents and businesses.

sections.label: SingPass and Compass outage concerns
sections.summary: A second outage hit SingPass and Compass, prompting IT professionals to express concerns about gateway systems and the national digital identity system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Recently, a second outage hit SingPass and the Complementarity Assessment Framework (ComPass).

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This prompted some IT professionals to express concerns about the robustness of the gateway systems and their impact on our new national digital identity system.

sections.label: E-registration plan for elections
sections.summary: An e-registration plan for future election was unveiled last May.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, an e-registration plan for future election was unveiled last May.

sections.label: Corruption Perception Index ranking
sections.summary: Transparency International released its annual Corruption Perception Index last month, an improvement over last year's 7th ranking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, last month, Transparency International released its annual Corruption Perception Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is an improvement over last year's ranking when she emerged 7th.

sections.label: Extra-territoriality corruption provisions introduced 1966
sections.summary: In 1966 extra-territoriality provisions made Singapore Citizens liable for corruption offences committed overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 1966, recognising that in a small country like Singapore, strict territorial limits would be insufficient to address potential mischief, the extra-territoriality provisions making Singapore Citizens liable for the offence of corruption overseas was introduced.

sections.label: Expanding extra-territoriality to corporations
sections.summary: The extra-territoriality provisions in the PCA would be expanded to include corporations registered in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, to expand that extra-territoriality provisions in PCA to include corporations registered in Singapore.

sections.label: Keppel penalty in Petrobras scandal
sections.summary: Keppel received a combined penalty of US$422 million in the US, Brazil and Singapore over Petrobras bribery corruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, recently, Keppel was given a combined total penalty of US$422 million in the US, Brazil and Singapore arising from their acts of corruption in the Petrobras bribery scandal in Brazil.

sections.label: Anti-corruption disclosure among listed companies
sections.summary: Of 606 listed companies surveyed, only 8.7% disclosed anti-corruption policies and practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to Assoc Prof Lawrence Loh's "Findings on the Singapore Governance and Transparency Index 2017", it seems that out of 606 listed companies surveyed which had released annual reports for their financial years ending 31 December 2016, only 8.7% had disclosed relevant policies and practices relating to anti-corruption.

sections.label: Reviewing company regulations and penalties
sections.summary: SGX rules require comply-or-explain governance; the Government should review regulations and consider inspections and penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In any event, the Singapore Exchange (SGX) rules only require listed companies to comply with the Code of Corporate Governance on a "comply or explain" basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is timely for the Government to review and enhance existing company regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should consider having inspections and subject non-compliance to penalties on the shoulders of the companies, directors and audit committee members.

sections.label: Auditing and disclosure in listed companies
sections.summary: The passage asks whether listed companies properly audit large payments, disclose related-party transactions and have diverse boards.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In practice, do publicly listed companies, particularly Government-linked ones, properly audit payments of large sums of money over a long period of time?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there full, frank and meaningful disclosure of related-party transactions?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there a diverse board of directors, composed of competent directors who are more than just a mere rubber stamp for key decisions?

sections.label: Corporate governance stewardship review
sections.summary: The speaker asks MAS whether listed companies comply with stewardship obligations, noting a review of the Code of Corporate Governance is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, finally, are appropriate stewardship obligations and principles that guide engagement with investors complied with by these listed companies?

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These questions are important, Mr Chairman, and I pose this to the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) in particular, because we understand that there is a review of the Code of Corporate Governance, as we have heard earlier, that is going on at the moment.

sections.label: SNDGG formation and coordination
sections.summary: The formation of SNDGG last year, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, has made strategy execution more coordinated and responsive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The formation of SNDGG last year, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, has enabled us to be even more coordinated and responsive in the execution of our strategy.

sections.label: SingPass mobile app launch
sections.summary: A SingPass mobile app will be launched in the second half of this year to support seamless, convenient and secure digital transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Both are essential if we are to achieve seamless, convenient and secure digital transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will launch the SingPass mobile app in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Secure digital identity and MyInfo
sections.summary: A secure digital identity lets citizens share data safely, with 70 Government services and 30 banking services already linked to MyInfo.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: A secure digital identity will also enable our citizens to share data safely and securely with other organisations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This point is important because we have already linked 70 Government services and 30 banking services to MyInfo.

sections.label: Faster bank account processing
sections.summary: Processing time to open new bank accounts and credit card applications has been reduced by 80%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For instance, the processing time to open new bank accounts and credit card applications has been reduced by 80%.

sections.label: PayNow Corporate and SGQR code
sections.summary: PayNow Corporate will launch this year for B2B and B2C payments, and the national SGQR code standard will be promoted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This will surely be more efficient than having to bank a cheque.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This year, we will also launch PayNow Corporate, which will enable businesses to link their bank accounts to their Unique Entity Numbers (UENs).

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In other words, this will now become business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will be promoting the adoption of the Singapore Quick Response (SGQR) code, which will be a national QR code standard.

sections.label: App for families with young children
sections.summary: In June 2018 an app called Moments of Life (Families) will let parents register births, apply for Baby Bonus, view records and search preschools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In June 2018, we will release an app for Singaporean couples starting a family or with children aged six and below.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will call this app – and we have not thought of a better name yet – "Moments of Life (Families)".

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It will allow parents, when they have a new baby, to register the baby's birth online, apply for Baby Bonus, view medical appointments and immunisation records and search and register interest for preschools.

sections.label: Critical ICT security requirements
sections.summary: The Government sets stringent reliability and resilience requirements for critical ICT systems and uses a security-by-design approach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Government imposes stringent reliability and resilience requirements for all our critical ICT systems, and we adopt a "security-by-design" approach to building this infrastructure.

sections.label: Smart Nation beyond technology deployment
sections.summary: The Smart Nation must expand opportunities, improve quality of life, enhance jobs and raise salaries, not just deploy technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: At its core, the Smart Nation is more than just the deployment of technology but really must expand opportunities and improve the quality of life, enhance jobs and raise salaries.

sections.label: Problem statements and TRANS Grant
sections.summary: The Government can give the private sector or research institutes a problem statement, and there is a TRANS Grant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This basically allows the Government to go to the private sector or to the research institutes, set out a problem statement and let the companies offer solutions based on their own expertise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We also have a grant called the Translational Research and Development for Application to Smart Nation (TRANS) Grant.

sections.label: Public ideas and nobody left behind
sections.summary: The public and industry are invited to contribute ideas through Ideas!, while ensuring nobody is left behind regardless of age, background, linguistic ability and special needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We invite the public and industry to contribute more ideas, more solutions, novel solutions, especially through Ideas!, which is a whole-of-Government crowdsourcing portal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Zaqy Mohamed, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Saktiandi Supaat that we must push ahead with digital technology but, at the same time, we must make sure nobody gets left behind, regardless of age and background and, I am also inclined to say, linguistic ability and special needs.

sections.label: Digital Government Blueprint release
sections.summary: The vision is a Government digital to the core, with a Digital Government Blueprint to be released in mid-2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Our vision is to be a Government that is digital to the core.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will release a Digital Government Blueprint in the middle of 2018.

sections.label: Business grants portal launch
sections.summary: A portal launched in January 2017 brings different Government agencies' business grant applications to one interface.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Launched in January 2017 at www.businessgrants.gov.sg, it brings different Government agencies' business grant applications to one interface.

sections.label: Business engagement streamlines applications
sections.summary: Engagement with businesses streamlined the application process by at least 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The engagement with businesses streamlined the application process by at least 15%.

sections.label: SingHealth paper MCs 2017
sections.summary: At SingHealth institutions alone, more than 1.1 million paper MCs were issued in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: At SingHealth institutions alone, more than 1.1 million paper MCs were issued in 2017.

sections.label: Centre of Excellence IT Smart Systems
sections.summary: A Centre of Excellence in IT and Smart Systems will be developed within the Government, with capability centres in several fields.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To achieve this, we will be developing a Centre of Excellence in IT and Smart Systems within the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Centre of Excellence will have capability centres in a number of fields: data science and AI, application design, development and deployment, ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity and sensors and the Internet of Things (IoT).

sections.label: Smart Nation Scholarship technical talent
sections.summary: A Smart Nation Scholarship will launch later this year to attract technologists for a technical leadership career in the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Government will ensure that there is sufficient technical talent like Rong Hwa and Zui Young to achieve our Smart Nation ambitions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will launch a Smart Nation Scholarship later this year to attract passionate and capable technologists to the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This scholarship aims to attract and groom a pool of talent for a technical leadership career in the Public Service.

sections.label: ELD e-registration next election
sections.summary: ELD conducted road shows and planned e-registration at some constituencies during PE 2017, and now plans it at the next election.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If I may inform the House, ELD had actually conducted road shows and planned to introduce e-registration at a few constituencies during PE 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: However, as PE 2017 was not contested, ELD's current plan is to implement e-registration of voters at the next election.

sections.label: Singapore corruption perceptions index ranking
sections.summary: Singapore was ranked 6th out of 180 countries in Transparency International's 2017 Corruption Perceptions Index, which the passage says shows the effectiveness of its anti-corruption framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The latest Transparency International of Corruption Perceptions Index of 2017 where Singapore was ranked 6th out of 180 countries was again testament to the effectiveness of our anti-corruption framework.

sections.label: CPIB private sector anti-corruption guide
sections.summary: In 2016 CPIB published PACT, a guide for Singapore businesses to develop and implement an anti-corruption framework within their companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In 2016, CPIB published a guide book for private sector use, called Practical Anti-Corruption (PACT), a guide for businesses in Singapore which sets out to guide business owners in developing and implementing an anti-corruption framework within their companies.

sections.label: ISO 37001 anti-bribery standard launch
sections.summary: The Singapore Standard ISO 37001 on Anti-Bribery Management Systems was launched in April 2017 at a seminar organised by CPIB with SPRING Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Singapore Standard ISO 37001, Anti-Bribery Management Systems, was subsequently launched in April 2017 in a seminar organised by CPIB, in partnership with SPRING Singapore.

sections.label: Review of Prevention of Corruption Act
sections.summary: A review of the PCA would engage different stakeholders and include public consultation, and all MPs will have the opportunity to contribute feedback at the appropriate juncture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A review of PCA is an important undertaking and would include the comprehensive engagement of different stakeholders and a public consultation to ensure that feedback is solicited in an exhaustive, comprehensive and wide-ranging manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It goes without saying that all MPs will have the opportunity to contribute their feedback and suggestions at the appropriate juncture as we seek to enhance our legislative tools to fight corruption.

sections.label: MAS supervisory approach on culture
sections.summary: MAS' supervisory approach has three prongs: promoting a culture of trust and ethical behaviour among FIs, monitoring and assessing their culture and conduct, and enforcing against misconduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In fact, this has become an increasingly important dimension in MAS' supervisory approach, which comprises three prongs: first, promote a culture of trust and ethical behaviour amongst FIs; second, monitor and assess FIs’ culture and conduct; and third, enforce against misconduct by FIs or their employees whenever necessary.

sections.label: MAS guidelines on individual accountability
sections.summary: MAS will soon consult on new guidelines to strengthen individual accountability and conduct across the financial industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS will soon be consulting on new guidelines to strengthen individual accountability and conduct across the financial industry.

sections.label: MAS enforcement actions outcomes
sections.summary: MAS enforcement actions have led to removal of directors or executive officers, composition fines, licence revocations and referral for criminal prosecution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The enforcement actions taken by MAS in recent years have led to the removal of directors or executive officers, composition fines, revocation of licences of FIs, as well as referral to the public prosecutor for criminal prosecution.

sections.label: Corporate Governance Council set up
sections.summary: MAS set up the Corporate Governance Council last year to review the Code.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS set up the Corporate Governance Council last year to review the Code.

sections.label: OECD Guidelines and Council recommendations
sections.summary: Some OECD disclosure guidelines are in the Securities and Futures Act and SGX listing rules, and the Council's recommendations are undergoing public consultation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: On the OECD Guidelines mentioned by Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan, some of the guidelines related to disclosures are already in the Securities and Futures Act and SGX listing rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The SGX listing rules also contain other important safeguards that deal with self-dealing risk arising from related party transactions and require listed companies to put in place robust and effective internal controls to address finance, operational and compliance risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The recommendations of the Council are now undergoing public consultation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Council will carefully evaluate the feedback received before making its final recommendations to MAS, which will, in turn, issue a revised Code in the later part of this year.

sections.label: Total amount each year
sections.summary: Added together, the amount is about $3 billion each year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If you add them all up, it is about $3 billion each year.

sections.label: TFR below replacement level
sections.summary: TFR has been below the replacement level of 2.1 for about 40 years and has stabilised at around 1.2 since 15 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The first is that TFR has been below the replacement level of 2.1 for about 40 years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And the second is that it has stabilised at around 1.2 since 15 years ago.

sections.label: South Korea support programme results
sections.summary: South Korea's extensive support programme did not achieve the same results as the countries it drew inspiration from, so financial and legislative support alone is not enough.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But I would say that based on my recollection, we did highlight that in the case of South Korea, there is a very extensive programme of support and it, too, has not achieved the same results as the countries that it drew inspiration from when designing those support programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, the upshot is that we cannot conclude that financial, legislative support alone is enough.

sections.label: 360-degree feedback for senior officers
sections.summary: 360-degree feedback is implemented broadly across senior officers and PSD will extend it to all senior officers in the next two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The 360-degree feedback: today, it has been implemented quite broadly across senior officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: PSD, in the next two, three years, will extend it to all senior officers.

sections.label: Unpaid leave and paternity leave utilisation
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng asked whether unpaid leave for unplanned emergencies can be legislated, but even with legislation utilisation is only 46%, and South Korea's legislated paternity leave utilisation is about 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether the unpaid leave for unplanned emergencies can be legislated.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But as Mr Seah Kian Peng pointed out, even with legislation, the utilisation is only 46%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When you consider that South Korea legislates paternity leave, in fact, of a much longer duration than we have, the utilisation is, if I am not mistaken, just about 2%.

sections.label: Fertility success rates by age
sections.summary: For women aged 35 to 39 the success rate is 18%, and for ages 40 to 44 it is less than 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For women aged between 35 and 39, the success rate is 18%, in other words, less than one in five.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Once you cross into the next five-year band, from age of 40 to 44, it is less than 8%, which means less than one in 10.

sections.label: No change for now
sections.summary: There is concern about giving a misimpression of succeeding when the chance is very low, so for the time being there will be no change.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is something that is of great concern to us, whether we give the misimpression that there is a chance of succeeding even though that chance is very low.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, for the time being, there will be no change.

sections.label: SingPass mobile app biometric rollout
sections.summary: A question asks whether there is a timeline for rollout in Singapore, referring to the SingPass mobile app that will use the smartphone's biometric feature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Is there a timeline where this will be rolled out for Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I was simply referring to the SingPass mobile app that will make use of the biometric feature on your smartphone.
